Bug_Title: Custom serialization methods should have required signatures
Bug_Details:
Java offers a built-in serialization mechanism for classes that implement the Serializable interface. The developer can either rely on
Java’s default serialization and deserialization logic or implement custom methods for these tasks. The JVM will use methods such as readObject and writeObject to execute custom behavior. This only works, however, if these methods match exactly the expected
signatures. If they do not, the JVM will fall back to the default logic, resulting in unexpected behavior at runtime, while the developer believes
that the default logic has been overidden.
This rule raises an issue if an implementation of writeObject , readObject , readObjectNoData , writeReplace , or readResolve has an incorrect access modifier, return type, or is not static when it should be (and
vice-versa).
Bug_Explanation: The methods writeObject and readObject are intended to override the default serialization and deserialization process. However, they have incorrect access modifiers (they should be private) and signatures (they must match exactly with the expected serialization method signatures in Serializable interface). As a result, the JVM uses the default serialization logic instead of the custom implementations.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by attempting to validate the custom serialization logic of the CustomSerializationExample class. The assertEquals statement expects the custom serialization to append ' - Custom Write' and ' - Custom Read' to the data string, but due to incorrect method signatures, the default serialization logic is used instead, causing the test to fail.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that the test passed successfully (OK (1 test)), which means the expected and actual outputs matched, despite the incorrect signatures for custom serialization methods. Therefore, the test results do not confirm the bug was triggered.
